title: Contextual advantage implies limited distinguishability in any physical theory
summary: A central question in quantum information is whether a given set of states can provide an advantage in some information-processing task. We establish a universal connection between two such questions: how well a set of states can be discriminated, and whether it can power tasks whose advantage stems from generalized contextuality.
